data.reason: Review of attempt 5 (subagent reviewer on opus, triage 75) returned the ticket on one medium finding. F1: a change that only edits a test of product code under packages/core/src is never held to the mutation floor, because mutation.source_files() and mutation_ci.select() both drop test files. Ruud decided F1 is fixed in this ticket (attempt 6). Four lows: F2 is the killed-mutant RED form decided at clarify record 6, noted only. F3: the report shows not applicable for a failed measurement. F4: the Outcome quotes CI run 37077429429 with no record behind it. F5: docs-only edits after regression 70, settled by the qa check on tree 2fb9729e. F1's fix needs a test-to-source mapping in mutation.py and mutation_ci.py, which is a new plan, so the return goes to solution.

findings.claim: A change that only edits a test of product code under packages/core/src is never held to the mutation floor. source_files() drops test files, so the tdd gate asks for no measurement. mutation_ci.select() drops them too (test_only_test_files_select_nothing asserts this), so CI skips the job. Weakening the tests of money code is exactly the regression mutation testing exists to catch.
findings.failure_scenario: Assume src/fees/detect.ts scores 90 against the floor. A later ticket's slice names only packages/core/src/fees/detect.test.ts and deletes the boundary assertions. With nothing left under src, _require_mutation returns early and the gate advances without a measurement. CI's changed step writes any=false. The real score of detect.ts drops to 40, and no gate, CI job or kpi figure records it. Fix: map a named or changed test file to the source it tests (its sibling, or its directory) for both the gate and CI.
findings.rule_candidate: none: a selection rule in harness/mutation.py and harness/mutation_ci.py that only a test of source_files and select over a test-only change can catch

findings.claim: Any Killed mutant in a file the slice names makes a valid killed-mutant RED, including one killed by a test that existed before the slice, so for an already-tested file the RED shows nothing about the new behaviour being absent.
findings.failure_scenario: A slice extends an already-tested packages/core/src file; a mutation run before any new test exits 0 with mutants killed by the old tests and is accepted as the slice's RED. This is the form clarify record 6 decided, so it is noted rather than returned on.

findings.claim: _mutation() prints 'not applicable' for any measurement with a null score, including a failed run and one refused for a missing entry, and kpi.mutation() takes the latest measurement on the ticket whatever its attempt.
findings.failure_scenario: Attempt 2's measurement fails and is the last mutation record; attempt 3's plan names nothing under src. The sprint report shows 'not applicable' for a run the gate refused as measuring nothing.

findings.claim: The Outcome lists run 37077429429 on dfbc3b9 (25 seconds) under 'Check 48 measured it', but no journal record holds that run.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader checking the attempt-5 figure against check 48 does not find it; nothing in the journal ties the 25 s to an output hash.

findings.claim: The fingerprint changed after regression 70 through docs-only edits (workflow.md, README row, ticket Outcome), so the tree the tests passed on is not the reviewed tree.
findings.failure_scenario: If any harness test read workflow.md, the reviewed tree would have no passing regression behind it. Today the change is prose only.
